topic.title: leap-year finder
topic.description: Any can find if a year is leap-year or not.

learningNotes.whatILearned: A leap year is every fourth year — except every hundredth, and except every fourth hundredth, which *is* one.
learningNotes.challenges: I never checked the year I read, so an empty answer tests whatever was on the stack against the leap-year rule.
learningNotes.nextSteps: Check the read, and write the rule itself in a comment above the conditions — the rule is the content here, and the code should carry it.

files.description: Any can find if a year is leap-year or not.

misconceptions: `scanf` returns how many items it read — the value is only ever set if you check that, so a missing answer leaves the variable untouched
The century rule is the exception to the four-year rule, and it has to come first: 400 divides by 400, so it must be tested before the 100 rule excludes it
engine.review:
**The rubric I used**

There is no task sheet for this one — it was written before the engine
existed, so there was nothing to grade it against. I graded the file on the
three things that have always mattered here:

- **40 — it runs.** It compiles or interprets without an error.
- **30 — it is right.** The output is what it claims to produce.
- **30 — it explains itself.** Comments say *why*, not *what*.

**40 + 30 + 5 = 75%**

**What is solid**

The rule is complete, and most people get this wrong. It checks `y % 400 == 0` first — so 2000 and 2400 are leap years — and only then `y % 4 == 0 && y % 100 != 0`, which catches 2024 but rejects 1900. I ran both: 2024 prints *is a leap-year*, 1900 prints *is not a leap year*. Both right, and 1900 is exactly the case that separates a real rule from a `y % 4 == 0` shortcut. It compiles clean.

**What is not**

The year is read without being checked, and the file has no comment at all — which is a shame, because *the rule* is the content of this program. `y % 400 == 0` is not code, it is the sentence 'except every hundredth, and except every fourth hundredth, which is one'. That sentence should be in the file.

**The one thing to fix first**

Write the rule above the code:

```c
/* A leap year is every 4th year, except every 100th,
   except every 400th - which is one after all. */
```

The comment is not decoration here. It *is* the lesson, and the conditions are just the rule written in C.
